name: URL Encode and Decode
task: Encode or decode a web address
tagline: Make text safe for a web address, read an encoded one, or take an address apart.
description: Percent-encode or decode text for web addresses, or split a URL into its parts and query parameters. Free, and nothing leaves your browser.

specs.Engine: Your browser's built-in encodeURIComponent and encodeURI
specs.Text: UTF-8, so accents and emoji work
specs.Works offline: Yes, once the page has loaded

faq.q: What is the difference between a part and a whole address?
faq.a: Choose "one part" for a single value, like a search word. It also changes / ? & = # and : so they cannot break the address. Choose "a whole address" to keep those characters as they are.

faq.q: Why does my text have %20 in it?
faq.a: A % followed by two hex digits stands for one byte. %20 is a space, and %C3%A9 is the letter é. Decode the text to read it.

faq.q: Is + a space or a plus?
faq.a: In a query string or form, + often means a space. Everywhere else it is a plus sign. Tick "Read + as a space" when you decode form data.
A % must be followed by two hex digits, like %20. A lone % or a cut-off code such as %E0%A4 cannot be read. Write a real % sign as %25.
